relations.myth: Typhon kills Heracles during his journey toward Libya
relations.note: Typhon kills the Tyrian Heracles while he travels toward Libya.

relations.myth: Iolaus revives Heracles with a quail
relations.note: Iolaus restores the dead Tyrian Heracles using a quail beneath his nose.

relations.myth: Hannibal and Philip's divine treaty witnesses
relations.note: Heracles and Iolaus jointly appear among the gods guaranteeing the Carthaginian treaty.
The Greek-form genealogy names Zeus as father of the Tyrian Heracles.
The Greek-form genealogy names Asteria as mother of the Tyrian Heracles.

relations.myth: Hiram renews their paired Tyrian temples
relations.note: Hiram constructs or renews paired temples for Heracles-Melqart and Astarte.
Later scholarship infers a couple from paired cults, without direct marriage evidence.
Cypriot inscriptions attest the locally fused compound deity Eshmun-Melqart.
An Ebusus temple dedication attests the compound divine name Resheph-Melqart.
Greek and bilingual evidence explicitly identifies Melqart with the ancient Tyrian Heracles.

relations.myth: Divine politics during Alexander's siege of Tyre
relations.note: Apollo's bound statue appears amid the dispute over sacrifice to Tyrian Heracles.

relations.myth: Dionysus encounters and praises the Tyrian Heracles
relations.note: Dionysus encounters and praises Melqart's syncretized cosmic form in Nonnus.
Tyros demands a robe matching the purple color produced by Melqart's dog.
